question: How did criterion 2 get its final form?

revisions.statement: Selectivity (real - control) at the best layer
Selectivity (real - control) at the best layer

revisions.threshold: control's max balanced accuracy over layers does not exceed the 95th percentile of 10,000 redrawn mappings
revisions.note: A leak bound, not a selectivity floor: under a type-disjoint split the control task's ceiling is chance. Drafted as 0.50 ± 0.03 (b9c861b); replaced before the push because ±0.03 fires 59–80% of the time with no leak (61bf29e).

answer:
Criterion 2 went through three registered revisions.

**Revision 1** (commit 12a0349, 2026-08-22) defined it as a selectivity floor: real minus control accuracy at the best layer had to be ≥ 0.10 [crit-rev1-2].

**Revision 2** (commit c7323d0, the same day) kept the statement but marked the 0.10 threshold "provisional" [crit-rev2-2]. The rows don't say why.

**Revision 3** (commit cb09c9d, 2026-09-26) is the final form. It changed the criterion from a selectivity floor to a leak bound: "Control task shows no leak." The control task's maximum balanced accuracy across layers must not exceed the 95th percentile of 10,000 redrawn mappings [crit-rev3-2]. The note explains the reasoning: under a type-disjoint split, the control task's ceiling is chance, so the criterion should test for leakage rather than set a selectivity floor [crit-rev3-2]. The revision cites Hewitt & Liang 2019, §2.3 [crit-rev3-2].

Before that version was pushed, a draft (b9c861b) used a fixed band of 0.50 ± 0.03. It was replaced (61bf29e) because a ±0.03 band would fire 59–80% of the time even with no leak [crit-rev3-2]. The permutation-based 95th-percentile threshold replaced it.
